So the request has:
```
GET / HTTP/1.1\r\n
Long: one\r\n
 two\r\n
Host: localhost\r\n
\r\n
```

The `Long` header value is `one\r\n two` (with line folding). According to HTTP spec (RFC 7230), obsolete line folding means that a header value can be continued on the next line with a CRLF followed by whitespace (space or tab). The continuation should be removed and the lines concatenated.

So the expected behavior is that `Long: one\r\n two` should be parsed as `Long: one two`.
